notes: Separate from .claude/modules.json (scope UI_ONLY), which is complete. Read .claude/saas/subscriptions.md §0 before starting: it is the scope permission this phase runs under. Work one module at a time in dependency order; a module is completed only when its database, backend, API, frontend integration, tests and audit entries are all in place.

modules.name: Tenant Foundation
modules.notes: Tenant model (id, name, slug, status, owner, timestamps) with unique slug. Tenant context derived from the authenticated server session, never from a client-supplied tenantId. Tenant-scoped query boundary and indexes on every tenant-owned table (courses, lessons, students, instructors, enrollments, certificates). Backfill migration that makes the existing single academy tenant #1 and assigns every existing record to it. Enforcement stays behind a flag until the backfill is verified. The existing 'admin' role is NOT renamed to tenantAdmin in this module.
doneWhen: Every tenant-owned table has a tenant FK and a tenant-scoped index
Changing an id in a URL cannot read or mutate another tenant's record
Existing records all carry a valid tenant relationship before enforcement is switched on
Cross-tenant access tests pass

modules.name: Plan Tables & Versioning
modules.notes: Database-backed plans replacing the in-memory fixtures from LMS-019: name, code (unique), description, status (draft/active/archived), displayOrder, monthlyPrice, annualPrice, currency, trialDays, archivedAt. Immutable/versioned commercial configuration so a price edit never rewrites a historical subscription or invoice. Money moves to the smallest currency unit (paise) in this module, in one deliberate migration — the prototype stores whole rupees. Port validatePlan from packages/domain/src/subscription.ts to the API and keep the two in sync.
doneWhen: Plan codes are unique at the database level
An archived plan cannot be chosen for a new subscription but existing ones keep it
Editing a plan's price leaves every historical record's terms untouched
Amounts are integers in the smallest currency unit throughout

Produce the §42 plan enforcement matrix as the source of truth, with every permission key verified against packages/domain/src/permission.ts. No plan-name checks anywhere in the codebase.

The enforcement matrix is written down and every permission key in it is real
A plan's features and limits are rows, not code

modules.name: Entitlement Service
modules.notes: getTenantEntitlements, hasFeature, getLimit, getUsage, canConsume as the single way any module asks about a plan. Authorization order is fixed: authenticated -> role/permission -> tenant isolation -> subscription/entitlement -> operation. Entitlement never replaces authorization; both must pass (admin permission courses.edit = true AND entitlement courses.manage = false => DENIED). No controller reads subscription tables directly.
doneWhen: No controller queries subscription or plan tables directly
Permission-denied and entitlement-denied are distinguishable in the error model
Unit tests cover both-pass, permission-only and entitlement-only cases

modules.name: Subscription Model & State Machine
modules.notes: Subscription table (tenantId, planId + version, status, billingCycle, currency, amount, period start/end, cancelAtPeriodEnd, canceledAt, cancellationReason, gracePeriodEndAt, provider references, timestamps) and the seven statuses trialing/active/past_due/paused/canceling/canceled/expired. Transitions enforced in the backend; an arbitrary status write is refused. Subscription lifecycle event log written on every transition, with tenant, subscription, actor/source, event, timestamp and metadata. Document the exact allowed transitions before production.
doneWhen: A status can only change through a named transition, never by direct write
Every transition writes a lifecycle event
Unit tests cover every edge of the state machine, including refused transitions

modules.name: Trials & Grace Period
modules.notes: Trial configuration from the plan; trialStartAt, trialEndAt and expiry decided entirely server-side — the frontend clock is never trusted. Repeat trials for the same tenant are prevented unless explicitly allowed. Grace period after a failed payment with a configurable duration, stored timestamps and stored reasons: past_due -> retry -> success/active, or retries exhausted -> grace -> restricted/expired.
doneWhen: Changing the client clock cannot extend a trial
A tenant cannot start a second trial unless the rule allows it
Grace duration is configuration, not a constant in code
Trial-expiry and grace-expiry unit tests pass

modules.name: Upgrade, Downgrade, Cancellation & Reactivation
modules.notes: Write down and implement the upgrade policy: immediate vs next-cycle, proration, effective date, payment requirement, when entitlements activate. Start with the safe model — entitlements activate only after confirmed payment, never on a frontend callback. Downgrade does not delete data: it takes effect per policy (usually next period), existing data stays, new usage beyond the new limit is restricted, and the tenant is told about the conflict. Cancel immediately or at period end, resume before the effective date; record actor, timestamp, reason and effective date. A fully canceled subscription is replaced by a new one rather than mutated.
doneWhen: The upgrade policy is documented before it is coded
A downgrade with usage over the new limit keeps the data and restricts new usage
Cancel/resume records actor, timestamp, reason and effective date
Upgrade and downgrade unit tests pass, including the limit-conflict case

modules.name: Money, Tax & Currency
modules.notes: All monetary arithmetic in the smallest currency unit with integers; no floating point in any financial total. The client never controls the payable amount — the server calculates it from the plan. Tax kept separate from base pricing (type, percentage, amount, inclusive flag, billing address, GST/registration where applicable), with no country-specific rules baked into generic subscription logic. Currency belongs to the price/subscription/invoice context; INR first, but the model must not block future currencies.
doneWhen: No float arithmetic reaches a stored total
A client-supplied amount is ignored and the server figure is used
Tax calculation unit tests pass
Adding a second currency needs no schema change

modules.name: Payment Records & Invoices
modules.notes: Immutable payment records (tenantId, subscriptionId, provider, providerPaymentId, amount, currency, status pending/paid/failed/refunded/partially_refunded, failureCode, failureMessage, paidAt, refundedAt) — a successful payment is never overwritten to represent a later event. Invoices with unique invoice numbers, billing period, subtotal, tax, total, status and provider reference; a plan change never rewrites a historical invoice. Payment methods stored only as provider-safe references plus masked display metadata (Visa •••• 4242, UPI) — never raw card details. Refunds are separate financial events, full or partial, and never delete the original payment. No destructive cascades.
doneWhen: No code path updates or deletes a paid payment
Invoice numbers are unique at the database level
No raw card data exists anywhere in the schema or logs
A refund leaves the original payment row intact

modules.name: Payment Provider Abstraction
modules.notes: A PaymentProvider interface (createCustomer, createSubscription, cancelSubscription, pauseSubscription, resumeSubscription, changePlan, createPayment, refundPayment, verifyWebhook) with one adapter chosen from the business requirement — do not integrate two gateways without one. Implements the §43 payment flow end to end, with the rule that a frontend success callback alone never activates a subscription, and the §44 failed-payment flow. Credentials come from secrets, never from the repository.
doneWhen: The LMS contains no direct gateway SDK call outside the adapter
Activating a subscription requires a verified provider event, not a browser callback
The failed-payment path records the failure and moves to past_due
No secret is committed

modules.name: Webhooks & Idempotency
modules.notes: POST /webhooks/:provider/subscription. Every event: verify the signature, validate the payload, identify the event, enforce idempotency, persist the receipt, update internal state transactionally, record audit information, return the right response. An unsigned webhook is never trusted. Webhook events persisted with provider, providerEventId, eventType, receivedAt, processedAt, status and payload reference, under a unique constraint on provider + providerEventId, so a replayed event repeats no side effect. Lifecycle events written from webhook processing, not from the UI.
doneWhen: A forged or unsigned webhook is rejected
The same providerEventId delivered twice causes exactly one state change
Webhook state updates are transactional
Forged-webhook, duplicate-webhook and replay tests pass

modules.name: Usage Tracking & Enforcement
modules.notes: Usage for learners, instructors, courses, storage, admin accounts and live sessions, with a documented decision per metric (live-calculated, cached, counter-based or reconciled). Concurrency-safe: two simultaneous requests must not both pass a check against the same stale usage and push the tenant over a hard limit. Restricted mode on expiry with per-operation policies for read, create, update, publishing, live classes, advanced reports, storage and learner/instructor creation — existing data stays per policy and the tenant is shown an upgrade prompt rather than a blank wall.
doneWhen: A concurrency test cannot exceed a hard limit
Each metric's calculation strategy is written down
Restricted mode blocks creation without destroying access to existing data
Usage enforcement integration tests pass

modules.name: Background Jobs
modules.notes: trial-expiry-check, subscription-renewal-check, past-due-retry, grace-period-expiry, scheduled-cancellation, usage-reconciliation, webhook-retry and invoice-generation. Every job idempotent, retryable, observable and safe to run more than once — running a job twice must not double-charge, double-cancel or double-notify. Reuse the existing scheduler from the notification and live-class work (phases F10–F12) rather than adding a second one.
doneWhen: Running each job twice in a row changes nothing the second time
Job failures are observable
The scheduler is the existing one, not a new mechanism

Tenant Admin can never manage platform plans or another tenant. Stable machine-readable errors (SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED, SUBSCRIPTION_PAST_DUE, SUBSCRIPTION_EXPIRED, FEATURE_NOT_INCLUDED, LIMIT_REACHED, PAYMENT_REQUIRED, PAYMENT_FAILED, PLAN_UNAVAILABLE, INVALID_SUBSCRIPTION_STATE) that never leak provider or database internals.

Every error is one of the documented codes

System and provider events identify themselves as such rather than borrowing a human actor. Observability for payment failures, webhook failures, subscription state changes, job failures, entitlement failures and limit violations. modules.name: Multi-Gateway Payments & Runtime Gateway Configuration
modules.notes: Product decision D11 (23 Sep 2026): more than one payment gateway, chosen at runtime by the Super Admin. A provider-neutral PaymentProvider with a registry and factory (Razorpay, VyaparGateway, and room for more) that subscription, invoice and payment logic depend on. Gateway credentials encrypted at rest in the database (PaymentGatewayConfig), the key a deployment secret, never returned or logged. Exactly one active gateway, enabled and configured; switching it affects only new payment attempts — an invoice keeps the gateway its first checkout used, and confirmations, webhooks, refunds and reconciliation always use the gateway recorded on the order or payment. Super Admin API and screen to configure, enable or disable, test and activate gateways, all audited. Razorpay moves from environment variables to the database. VyaparGateway is implemented only from its actual API contract.
doneWhen: Business logic reaches a gateway only through the provider abstraction and factory
Gateway credentials are encrypted at rest, never in source, env files, API responses, logs or audit entries
Exactly one active gateway, enabled and configured, is enforced in the database and the API
Switching the active gateway affects only new payments; existing invoices, orders, webhooks and refunds keep their original gateway
Razorpay runs from database configuration with its webhook secret separate from its API secret
VyaparGateway is implemented from its actual API contract, with verified webhooks
Super Admin can configure, enable, disable, test and activate gateways; every change is audited
All existing payment, subscription, webhook, first-purchase and refund tests pass unchanged in behaviour
modules.blockedReason: VyaparGateway's API contract is not published. Its public pages describe two different, incomplete APIs: POST /api/v1/create_order on one, POST /v1/intents with GET /api/intents/{id}/status on another. Neither documents response fields, the authentication header, refunds, or exactly what the webhook signature (x-vyapargateway-signature, HMAC-SHA256) covers. The /docs endpoint returns Not Found, and there is no SDK. The full reference is only in the merchant dashboard. A human with a VyaparGateway merchant account must supply the API reference or OpenAPI spec, test-mode credentials, and the webhook signature scheme. Everything else in SAAS-017 is implemented and verified; VyaparGateway is registered as not implemented and cannot be configured, enabled or activated.

modules.name: Learner Assessment Integrity

Strip them from every learner-facing payload; return the attempt result to the learner only as the quiz showResults setting allows (Flutter B7); enforce the quiz time limit on the server rather than trusting client-reported duration; enforce assignment format and word limit on submit and refuse file ids the learner does not own. Backend only — no web or mobile change.

Staff endpoints still return the full quiz for authoring

modules.name: Academy Lifecycle & Provisioning

Build a transactional provisioning service (tenant, first admin with the permission catalogue, settings, levels, ranks, default certificate template — derived from what the LMS requires, not the demo seed), Super Admin endpoints to create, view, update, suspend, reactivate and archive an academy and read its users, subscription and usage, and enforce tenant status on every request. Deactivation keeps every row. Backend only.

Every lifecycle change is audited; slugs are validated and unique; the default academy cannot be archived
Tenant isolation, billing and existing Super Admin tests pass unchanged

modules.name: Sessions: Logout, Revocation & Account Self-Service
modules.notes: Flutter B1 and B3; docs/11 §24 known limitation. Tokens cannot be revoked and there is no logout endpoint, change-password or profile update for a signed-in account. Add server-side sessions carried in the token (sid) and checked on the per-request account read — POST /auth/logout, POST /auth/logout-all, change password (revokes every other session), profile update — and revoke sessions on password reset and deactivation. Tokens issued before this change stay valid until they expire, so existing web and mobile clients keep working. Refresh tokens (B2) are not added: they change the client contract and the 7-day lifetime stands.
doneWhen: POST /auth/logout revokes the calling token only; POST /auth/logout-all revokes every session of the account
Changing or resetting a password revokes the other sessions and requires the current password to change it
Profile update changes name only through a validated schema; email and role cannot be changed there
A revoked session answers 401 on every protected route
Pre-existing tokens without a session id still work until expiry
Auth rate limits cover the new endpoints

modules.name: Notification Delivery: Email Worker, Device Tokens & Push
modules.notes: Email is written to the outbox and never delivered, retried or given a final status; there is no device-token registration and no push transport (Flutter B4). Add an email delivery worker behind a transport abstraction (outbox/log today; SMTP when configured) with attempts, backoff, final status and deduplication; device-token registration and unregistration endpoints bound to the session; and a push dispatcher behind a provider abstraction that sends a hint (notification id and category) for in-app notifications the recipient’s preferences allow. An FCM provider needs Firebase credentials — that live verification is blocked until they exist.
doneWhen: Queued email is delivered by a scheduled worker with bounded retries, backoff, final status and an attempt count
The same message is not queued twice within its dedup window
POST/DELETE /notifications/devices register and remove a device token for the signed-in account, tenant-scoped, and sign-out removes the session’s tokens
Push delivery respects preferences and quiet hours, records its outcome, and never carries notification content beyond id and category
With no push provider configured, nothing fails and nothing is sent

modules.name: Job Leases & Multi-Instance Safety
modules.notes: The in-process scheduler runs every minute in every API process. With two instances each job would run twice at once. Add a database lease per job so only one instance runs a job at a time, taken atomically, expiring if its holder dies, and observable to the Super Admin.
doneWhen: Two schedulers running concurrently never run the same job at the same time
A lease held by a dead process expires and is taken over
